validationTargets.label: Workstation shell app
validationTargets.targetShape: multi-panel desktop workspace with docks, tabs, split views, and command discovery
validationTargets.notes: Closest to Aura-like or Spark-like desktop shell pressure, but still generic shared shell surface.

validationTargets.label: Detail and review app
validationTargets.targetShape: document, review, and approval surfaces with forms, detail rows, cards, notifications, and media fallback posture
validationTargets.notes: Exercises non-DAW productivity surfaces so workstation assumptions do not silently define all GPUI expectations.

validationTargets.label: Utility or tool window
validationTargets.targetShape: small focused tool with menus, settings, lists, and lightweight command or notification posture
validationTargets.notes: Exposes whether the shared layer assumes large workstation chrome or panel orchestration by default.

sharedLayerAssumptionsExposed: workstation-shell pressure must not become the default assumption for every GPUI app context
token-only GPUI readiness is insufficient proof of component ergonomics or host integration posture
focus, keyboard, and announcement semantics must be validated separately for workstation, productivity, and utility shapes
shared shell and composite layers must stay free of Loophole-specific DAW nouns and Underlay-specific wrapper expectations
layout persistence and command-discovery helpers must remain host-owned patterns rather than mandatory app architecture
requiredFollowUp: build or review at least one GPUI workstation-shaped adoption target
build or review at least one non-workstation GPUI target so shell assumptions are challenged
record any contract or package adjustments exposed by those targets instead of hiding them as app-local patches
currentBlockers: GPUI package surface is still token-only in this repo and does not yet provide shipped GPUI component crates.
No downstream GPUI app repos are present in this workspace for direct end-to-end validation.
Accessibility and interaction evidence for native GPUI surfaces still remains largely contract-level rather than runtime-proven.
